Okay, let’s gauge individual investor and public sentiment independently.

Should Jensen Huang remain CEO of $NVDA?

Regarding $NBIS earnings results:

To show you how fast they're growing... from Q2 to Q3: 

Revenue: $582.3M -> $980.8M (+68% QoQ)
Adjusted EBITDA: $236.2M -> $465.8M (+97% QoQ)
AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin: 49.7% -> 53.2%
Net Income: −$190.4M -> −$37.5M

ARR has reached $6.4B at the end of Sep. In terms of management commentary: 

- Since start of Q3, Nebius signed $12B+ of new contracts
- Average GPU pricing rose 20%+ sequentially, payback shortened from 22M -> 19M
- On Q3 deals, prepayments covered 100% of associated capex, up from 50–60% in Q2 (insane for financing)
- Contract value per MW exceeded $25M+ from Q3 up from ~$20M Q2 
- 5GW contracted power year end

With $10B of committed customer prepayments in 2026 and $17B-$20B in 2027. Now, prepayments and borrowing against existing contracts covers ~75-85% of 2027 capex. 

On subsidiaries:
1. Avride - 250 autonomous vehicles fleet, over 100,000 passenger rides (with companies like $UBER). Fully driverless robotaxi targeted H1 2027.
2. Toloka - Revenue doubled sequentially
3. Enterprise cloud - Databricks and Datadog selected Neibus. Along with a new agreement with Snowflake. 
4. Tavily - Over 3M developers now with $IBM post-training a core partner. 
5. ClickHouse - Nothing about new secondary valuations, but we can see valuations growing
6. TokenFactory - Contract value grew 17x sequentially

The primary negative I saw was that 2026 guidance is now on the lower end (near ~$3B), due to $MSFT capacity deliveries slipping to Q2 2027.

Apparently there was an execution miss with a third party partner DataOne. Temporary generators were retired amid permitting issues before enough $BE fuel cell capacity came online. 

Capex also increased in 2026 from $20B-$25B to $27B, while revising revenue expectations downward. 

So near-term unfortunate headwinds kinda reminiscent of AOI earnings; however long term I think Nebius will take care of you. 

For 2027 outlook:
- $12-13 billion revenue, capex of $40-45 billion, pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027.

Very operationally bullish, as seen with prepayments covering capex, GPU premiums increasing. Main downside is near-term execution risk from third parties, causing near-term delays and revenue recognition. 

Great quarter from Nebius overall.
@aleabitoreddit Why did it tank on these good news

So there's the positive fundamental long term outlook that I've interpreted. 

On the other hand, there's near term headwinds that I highlighted above, which markets are pricing in. 

Negatives I saw near term were $MSFT Vineland pushing back into Q2 2027, which delays revenue recognition. 

Alongside 2026/2027 capex hikes + downward revision of next quarter revenue. We've seen markets punish near term execution delays with $AAOI recently too. 

For long term, I don't see this earnings as negative, given 100% prepayments, compute prices going up, new contracts and their subsidiaries growing.

$NVDA Jensen Huang has now resigned.

Despite the overwhelming support worldwide and from his employees. 

This is an end of an era for Nvidia.
